positions.title: PhD in Management — Organisational Behaviour Field
positions.notes: Fully funded 5-year scholarship (tuition waiver + annual living stipend + research/conference funding + international health insurance). Dual campus: Fontainebleau (France) and Singapore. Organisational Behaviour field directly relevant to managerial control, HRM, and work organisation research. INSEAD is among the world's top-ranked business schools. Applications open September 2026 for mid-August 2027 intake. DEADLINE CORRECTED 17 Sept 2026: January 4, 2027 (open-one-way interview by Jan 6, 2027). Interview rounds: Jan–Mar 2027. GMAT/GRE mandatory (< 5 years old). Any bachelor's degree accepted; master's advantageous but not required. International students strongly encouraged.

positions.title: Doctoral Positions — IMPRS-SPCE (Economic Sociology & Political Economy)
positions.institution: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Societies (MPIfG) / University of Cologne / University of Duisburg-Essen
positions.notes: Application window opens December 2026 (exact deadline TBC — monitor imprs.mpifg.de/99889/calls-for-applications). 3.5-year doctoral programme (42-month contract + 6-month wrap-up). Focus: economic sociology, comparative/international political economy, organizational sociology. Strong comparative institutional and VoC alignment — MPIfG is the global centre for VoC and institutional analysis (Hall & Soskice's original institutional home). Research on how social and political structures shape economic action directly bridges to Bijneshwor's institutional framework. International applicants from Germany and abroad welcome; English is required. Up to 8 students admitted per year. Contact: mischa.stratenwerth@mpifg.de

Managerial control is Bijneshwor's core construct — strong alignment. Nordic institutional context. Job ID 305122. Monitor NHH for next cycle (expected Jan 2027).

scholarships.name: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS)
scholarships.notes: MOST URGENT DEADLINE — 1 Dec 2026, 12:00 noon HK time. CONFIRMED OPEN (17 Sept 2026): RGC page shows 'Open for application now! Please refer to call circular.' HKUST-specific: full application also due 1 Dec 2026 by 11:59 pm. HKU/CUHK regular deadline also 1 Dec 2026. Regular non-HKPFS deadline: 3 Jan 2027 (HKUST). HKU converts every HKPFS holder automatically to Presidential PhD Scholarship (Year 1 cash award + tuition waiver + guaranteed hall place). Bij's floor: HKD 31,000–33,500/month — HKPFS alone fails; HKPFS + university top-up clears it. Decline studentship-only fallback (~HKD 18,000–19,000/month) outright. Sociology route confirmed (no GMAT at any HK sociology dept). Active contacts: Yi-min Lin (HKUST, sent), Zhu Ling (CUHK, sent), Ladegaard (HKU, declined). Only one HKPFS application ever permitted across all HK universities. Critical open item: line up 2nd (CUHK: 3rd) academic referee — only Prof Flavio confirmed so far.
scholarships.eligibility: Outstanding candidates regardless of country of origin; must apply to HKUST / HKU / CUHK / PolyU etc. simultaneously. Highly competitive (~270 awarded from thousands).

scholarships.name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships
scholarships.amount: Full tuition waiver + monthly stipend (CHF 1,920–3,500 depending on level and canton)
scholarships.notes: URGENT — deadline ~Nov 10, 2026. Nepal is an eligible country. Swiss universities (St. Gallen, Zurich, Lausanne) have strong management, institutional, and comparative organization research. Aligns with Germanic/Nordic theory pillar in proposal. Applications opened 20 August 2026. Country-specific deadline for Nepal not explicitly confirmed on main SBFI page (17 Sept 2026 check) — verify with Swiss Embassy Kathmandu. Apply through Swiss Embassy in Kathmandu.
scholarships.eligibility: Open to applicants from 183 countries including Nepal. For PhD research and postdoc at Swiss universities. Apply through Swiss Embassy in Kathmandu.

scholarships.name: UNU-WIDER Visiting PhD Fellowship (September 2026 cycle)
scholarships.provider: United Nations University — World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER), Helsinki, Finland
scholarships.amount: EUR 2,100/month stipend + return travel grant + medical insurance (3-month residency in Helsinki)
scholarships.notes: MOST URGENT — deadline September 30, 2026 at 23:59 UTC+3 (13 days from 17 Sept 2026). Main page returned 403 on 17 Sept scan — confirmed open via globalsouthopportunities.com (published 1 Sept 2026). Highly aligned: explicitly for PhD research on developing economies, with priority to researchers from developing countries (Nepal qualifies). Bijneshwor's research on Nepalese institutional environment maps directly onto the 'developing economies' mandate. Three months in Helsinki gives access to UNU-WIDER's global development research network and Nordic institutional context. Qualitative methods explicitly welcomed. Applies as a visiting scholar supplement, not a degree programme — can be combined with ongoing PhD enrolment. Highly competitive (~1% success rate historically). Two cycles per year: March 31 and September 30 deadlines.
scholarships.eligibility: Currently enrolled PhD students conducting dissertation research on developing economies. Strong qualitative and/or quantitative analytical skills required. English proficiency required. Priority given to researchers from developing countries (Nepal qualifies), women researchers, and advanced-stage PhD students.
